parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows `minimumTokenResponseSchema = z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), ... })`. A computed key like `[z.string().toString()]]` evaluates to a literal property name (not a Zod catch-all), so when credential sync is enabled, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses this schema instead of e.g. refreshTokenResponseSchema. The parsed data then lacks real fields like expiry_date/refresh_token (and refresh_token is defaulted to the placeholder string "refresh_token"), while office365calendar's refreshAccessToken does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and persists it — leaving credentials without a valid expiry. The described mechanism matches the diff.
